title: Space Force orders two more Impulse Space vehicles for maneuvering demonstrations
summary: The U.S. Space Force has expanded a contract with Impulse Space by $28 million to include two additional vehicles, Victus Salo 2 and 3, for responsive-space maneuvering demonstrations. This follows an earlier award for similar missions.

title: Pentagon missile buildup changing the factory floor
summary: Startups are introducing commercial space technologies like software, robotics, and advanced manufacturing to the defense industry to accelerate missile production. This shift is driven by Pentagon pressure to rapidly scale up weapon manufacturing.

title: Space Command identifies capabilities it needs for the next space war
summary: U.S. Space Command has outlined the need for offensive capabilities to counter future space threats, specifically targeting the critical nodes of large satellite constellations. General Stephen Whiting has urged the industry to develop methods to disable such nodes in potential conflicts.

title: Golden Dome creates digital hub to expand commercial participation
summary: Golden Dome has launched a digital ecosystem hub to facilitate commercial participation by allowing companies to request information and submit ideas. This initiative aims to expand engagement with the space industry.

title: China’s iSpace raises first batch of series E funding for reusable rocketry
summary: Chinese reusable launch vehicle manufacturer iSpace has secured the first part of a Series E funding round, with additional fundraising still ongoing. The company aims to advance its reusable rocketry technology following a significant D++ funding round earlier.

title: One species, one planet: The moon is our ethical dress rehearsal for Mars
summary: The article discusses how the Moon serves as a crucial ethical and practical testing ground for future human missions to Mars. Bruce Jakosky and Scott Hubbard highlight the importance of pragmatic systems engineering in space exploration.

title: Firefly increases vehicle production even as launches lag
summary: Firefly Aerospace is increasing production of its launch vehicles due to strong demand, but this has not yet resulted in a higher launch rate.

title: U.S. expands missile production as Army seeks more depth in its arsenal
summary: The U.S. is increasing missile production to enhance its arsenal, with recent agreements involving Northrop, Lockheed, and L3Harris to expand capacity in propulsion, structures, and other critical supply chain areas.

title: Golden Dome faces 2027 funding cliff
summary: The Golden Dome program faces a funding cliff in 2027, with Gen. Michael Guetlein emphasizing the need for Congress to secure future financing as most initial funding is already allocated. The program's next phase remains uncertain without additional financial commitments.

title: National lab visit boosts NASA’s confidence in space nuclear propulsion mission
summary: NASA officials expressed confidence in launching a nuclear electric propulsion demonstration mission by the end of 2028 after visiting the national lab constructing the mission's reactor.

title: This year's 'Masters of the Universe' movie wasn't Hollywood's first attempt at capturing the power of He-Man; they tried back in 1987, and failed then too
summary: The 1987 attempt to make a He-Man movie failed due to bad timing, a studio in financial turmoil, and a film that didn't resemble the original cartoon. The recent 'Masters of the Universe' movie marks Hollywood's second attempt to bring the iconic character to the big screen.

title: Total solar eclipse 2026 thrills millions with a stunning cosmic spectacle (photos, video)
summary: A total solar eclipse on August 12, 2026, captivated millions as it traversed Greenland, Iceland, and Spain, showcasing stunning cosmic visuals captured in photos and videos.

title: Total solar eclipse 2026 has begun. Here are the first views of totality
summary: The total solar eclipse of 2026 has begun, with the first stunning images of totality showing the sun's atmosphere around the moon's silhouette. This celestial event has captivated observers worldwide.

title: Radiation-shielding vest aced Artemis I lunar test, could protect astronauts on moon and Mars missions
summary: A radiation-shielding vest successfully passed its Artemis I lunar test in 2022, demonstrating potential to protect astronauts during long-duration missions to the moon or Mars.

title: Farthest 'black hole star' ever found could help solve the James Webb Space Telescope's little red dot mystery
summary: A distant black hole star is providing evidence that these objects may explain the 'little red dot' mystery observed by the James Webb Space Telescope shortly after the Big Bang.

title: Green comet caught soaring over Namibia | Space photo of the day for Aug. 12, 2026
summary: A stunning space photo of a green comet over Namibia was featured as Space.com's photo of the day on Aug. 12, 2026. The image captivated astronomers and astrophotographers alike with its breathtaking beauty.

title: On this day in space! Aug. 12, 2005: Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter launched
summary: NASA launched the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter (MRO) mission on August 12, 2005. The MRO is a key spacecraft for studying Mars' surface and climate.

title: SpaceX wraps Starlink double header day with the launch of 24 Starlink satellites from California
summary: SpaceX completed two Starlink satellite launches in a single day, deploying 24 satellites from California on Aug. 11. This marks the second Starlink mission of the day, further expanding the company's global internet constellation.

title: A total solar eclipse will darken the sky for millions today! Here's what you need to know
summary: A total solar eclipse is occurring today, passing over Greenland, Iceland, and Spain. Details on timings, livestreams, and safety advice are available.

title: NASA Data Helps Commercial Space Plan Living Off Our Moon
summary: NASA data is being utilized by Lunar Station Corp. to aid in commercial space planning for lunar resource extraction, focusing on water and minerals like iron and titanium.

title: NASA Upgrades Vertical Motion Simulator for Modern Mission Needs
summary: NASA has upgraded its Vertical Motion Simulator to enhance its capabilities for modern mission needs, including spacecraft and lunar landing simulations. The simulator is the largest of its kind and now offers improved performance.

title: NASA Astronaut Mike Fincke Leaves NASA, Career Includes 4 Spaceflights
summary: NASA astronaut Mike Fincke is retiring after 30 years of service, having completed four spaceflights, 549 days in space, and nine spacewalks. His career significantly contributed to multiple chapters of NASA's history.

title: Pursuing a Dream of Working for NASA
summary: Lindsey Waitt has realized her childhood dream of working for NASA by joining the agency as a test project engineer for the Artemis launch team. Her role is crucial for NASA's missions aimed at returning humans to the lunar surface.

title: APOD: 2026 August 12 – Perseids over a Little Planet
summary: APOD features an image of the Perseids meteor shower over a 'little planet' perspective. The Astronomy Picture of the Day (APOD) is a daily showcase of cosmic images with expert explanations.

title: Quality Assessment Report Evaluates Polar Geospatial Center EarthDEM Elevation Products
summary: A quality assessment report has evaluated the Polar Geospatial Center's EarthDEM elevation products. The report, part of NASA's Commercial Smallsat Data Acquisition (CSDA) program, informs users about the quality of commercial Digital Elevation Models (DEMs).

title: What Is the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope? (Grades 5-8)
summary: The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope is NASA's newest astrophysics observatory designed to scan large sections of space and help astronomers study dark energy, dark matter, and exoplanets. It is intended for educational purposes, targeting students in grades 5-8.

title: NASA Completes Astronaut-Deployed Science Instrument for Lunar Surface
summary: NASA has completed the first payload designed for Artemis astronauts to deploy on the Moon's surface. The Lunar Environment Monitoring Station (LEMS) is ready for deployment near the lunar South Pole.

title: Amid failure, Wenchang celebrates milestone as China launches AI satellites and prepares for lunar south pole mission
summary: China's Wenchang Space Launch Site celebrated its 50th launch milestone while also experiencing a failure. The site launched AI satellites and is preparing for a lunar south pole mission.

title: Starbase Production lining up future vehicles
summary: SpaceX's Starbase production site is advancing the assembly of multiple Starship vehicles. The progress highlights preparations for future missions.

title: Launch Preview: Chinese failure opens busy international launch salvo
summary: The week of Aug. 10 saw four international launches across three countries following a Chinese failure. The busy launch schedule highlights global space activity despite setbacks.

title: Artemis progress building lunar return roadmap
summary: NASA has provided updates on the Artemis program, detailing progress in building a roadmap for returning humans to the Moon. The updates include commercial robotic lunar missions as part of the initiative.

title: Blue Origin working engine resolutions and dual pad future
summary: Blue Origin is nearing the end of its investigation into a catastrophic engine explosion. The company is also planning for a dual launch pad future.

title: Relativity Space engine integration milestone for Terran-R first stage
summary: Relativity Space has achieved a key milestone in integrating engines for the first stage of its reusable Terran-R rocket. This development advances the company's progress toward the rocket's maiden launch.

title: Crew-13 pilot reflects on career, training, and upcoming science ahead of flight to ISS
summary: NASA has moved up the launch date for the Crew-13 mission to the ISS. The Crew-13 pilot shared insights on their career, training, and upcoming scientific objectives.

title: While SpaceX recovers Ship 40, Ship 41 prepares for testing ahead of Flight 14
summary: SpaceX is recovering Ship 40 after its soft landing in the Indian Ocean, while Ship 41 prepares for testing ahead of Flight 14.

title: Launch Preview: Starlink, AST SpaceMobile, and Chinese missions fill launch manifest
summary: The first week of August is expected to be busy with multiple launches, including Starlink, AST SpaceMobile, and Chinese missions. The manifest highlights a significant number of space activities planned for this period.

title: Boeing’s Starliner set for potential 2026 cargo run to ISS
summary: Boeing's CST-100 Starliner spacecraft may conduct a cargo mission to the International Space Station (ISS) in 2026. CEO Kelly Ortberg mentioned ongoing redesign efforts for the spacecraft.

title: ESA Delivers: 50 years booklet
summary: The European Space Agency (ESA) has released a booklet celebrating 50 hallmark achievements over its 50-year history. This publication highlights key milestones and contributions in space exploration and technology.

title: How ESA mimics and models the 2026 total solar eclipse
summary: ESA is preparing to study the 2026 total solar eclipse by using artificial eclipse missions and computer simulations to observe the Sun's corona. This approach allows scientists to gather more data than a natural eclipse provides.

title: Your chance to run software in deep space on ESA's asteroid mission
summary: The European Space Agency is inviting European researchers and companies to run their software aboard the Hera mission, which will travel millions of kilometers into deep space. This is a rare opportunity to test software in a deep-space environment.

title: From drone flight to sounding rocket
summary: A student-developed radar retroreflector technology was tested for the first time using a drone at ESTEC, the European Space Agency’s technical centre in the Netherlands. This marks a transition from drone flight to sounding rocket applications.

title: Earth and Proba-3’s Coronagraph play hide and seek
summary: ESA's Proba-3 mission will demonstrate formation flying by having one satellite block the Sun to create an artificial solar eclipse for the other. This will allow the coronagraph to study the Sun's corona without interference.

title: Meet space startups at ESA’s Industry Space Days
summary: ESA's Industry Space Days event on September 16-17 will bring together space startups and the European space industry to exchange ideas, showcase capabilities, and explore collaborations. The event at ESA-ESTEC in the Netherlands aims to foster innovation and partnerships within the space sector.

title: The silicon brains steering next-generation antennas
summary: The article discusses advancements in silicon-based technology for next-generation antennas. These innovations are expected to enhance communication and data transmission capabilities in the space industry.

title: Plato's electronics ready for space
summary: ESA's PLATO spacecraft has completed critical electromagnetic compatibility tests in the Maxwell Test Chamber, confirming its electronics are space-ready. The mission is now cleared for launch on an Ariane 6 rocket in March 2027.

title: Test firing at brand new green chemical propulsion lab
summary: A new green chemical propulsion lab conducted its first test firing. This marks a significant step in developing environmentally friendly propulsion technologies for space missions.

title: Firefly Announces Record Q2 Results
summary: Firefly Aerospace reported its first-ever quarterly revenue exceeding $100 million, driven by new launch and defense contracts. The company announced these record Q2 results on Tuesday.

title: Guetlein: CR Could Mean ‘No Golden Dome…No Funding’
summary: A senior official warned that a Continuing Resolution (CR) could lead to funding shortages, potentially impacting major projects like the 'Golden Dome'. Without a resolution, critical funding may be unavailable.

title: Bill Spotlight: Space Superiority Readiness Act
summary: A bipartisan pair of senators introduced a bill to ensure U.S. military readiness for potential conflicts in space involving China. The legislation aims to enhance space superiority capabilities.

title: Rocket Lab Unveils GHOST on a Record Quarter
summary: Rocket Lab introduced GHOST, a deployable launch system for responsive global launches. The announcement coincided with a record quarter for the company.

title: Astrolight, ATMOS Partner on Laser Comms Reentry Demo
summary: Astrolight and ATMOS have partnered to conduct a laser communications demonstration onboard ATMOS' PHOENIX 2 reentry vehicle in 2027. This collaboration aims to advance reentry communication technologies using laser terminals.

title: MDA Space Will ‘Repurpose’ Canadarm3 For Lunar Surface
summary: MDA Space plans to adapt its Canadarm3 robotics technology for lunar surface operations following NASA's pause on the Gateway program. The company aims to leverage its microgravity robotics expertise for future Moon missions.

title: Europe’s IRIS2 Constellation Enters the Build Phase
summary: Europe's IRIS2 satellite constellation has entered the implementation phase after seven months of negotiations among the European Commission, ESA, EUSPA, and SpaceRISE. This marks a significant step toward building the constellation.

title: The Launch Crunch Just Made a ULA Sale Worth Revisiting
summary: The recent surge in launch demand has made ULA's sale a more attractive proposition. This highlights the growing importance of launch services in the space industry.

title: Redwire Books Starfall’s First Dedicated Mission
summary: Redwire subsidiary SpaceMD secured a contract to transport up to 32 mini-labs on a future SpaceX Starfall mission. This marks Redwire's first dedicated mission under its Starfall program.

title: Op-ed: Aging Weather Satellites Are Raising Risks for America. It’s Time for a Hybrid Solution.
summary: Aging weather satellites are increasing risks for the U.S., prompting a call for a hybrid solution to improve military weather data quality and availability.

title: Optus Completes First Part of Project Aurora
summary: Optus, an Australian telecommunications and satellite company, has completed the first phase of Project Aurora, a satellite life extension initiative.

title: Marlink to Acquire U.K. Defense Comms Specialist GRC
summary: Marlink is acquiring U.K.-based defense communications specialist GRC to strengthen its position in European government, defense, and critical infrastructure markets. The acquisition aims to enhance Marlink's capabilities in secure communications.

title: Space42 and Leonardo DRS to Boost UAE National Security
summary: Space42 and Leonardo DRS have signed a memorandum of understanding to enhance national security capabilities in the United Arab Emirates (UAE). Leonardo DRS will contribute its expertise as part of the agreement.

title: Rocket Lab Margins Under the Microscope Following 2Q Earnings
summary: Rocket Lab faced investor scrutiny over its margins following the release of its second-quarter earnings. The company's financial performance was closely analyzed in the space industry.

title: DamoTech Joins Space ISAC
summary: DamoTech has joined the Space Information Sharing and Analysis Center (Space ISAC) to contribute its expertise in advanced cybersecurity for the space sector. This move highlights the growing focus on security collaboration within the space industry.

title: U.S. Space Force Selects Voyager Technologies for Space-to-Space Communications Development Award
summary: The U.S. Space Force has selected Voyager Technologies to develop space-to-space communication capabilities under a new contract. This award marks a significant step in enhancing military space communications.

title: The Trump Administration Attempts to Fill an Empty FCC Seat Ahead of Midterm Elections
summary: The Trump Administration nominated FCC Chairman Brendan Carr for a fourth FCC seat ahead of midterm elections, after the commission operated with three members for nearly two years.

title: Arabsat Signs Digital Communications Infrastructure Deal with Libya Telecom and Technology (LTT)
summary: Arabsat has signed a deal with Libya Telecom and Technology (LTT) to develop Libya's digital communications infrastructure. The agreement aims to enhance connectivity for Libya's population of around 7.5 million people.

title: ALL.SPACE to Provide Hydra MAX Terminals to Aalyria
summary: ALL.SPACE has secured a contract to supply its Hydra MAX terminals to Aalyria for integration with their Spacetime orchestration software. The deployment aims to enhance Aalyria's satellite communication capabilities.

title: Catalyst Completes Infrastructure EO Analysis Pilot Program with UK Rail Operator
summary: Catalyst (PCI Geomatics) completed a 12-week pilot program with Network Rail to analyze weather-driven risks using Earth Observation (EO) analytics. The collaboration focused on infrastructure EO analysis for Britain's railway network.
